title: Breadcrumb and contextual heading strategy + wireframe notes
content:
Context / why this doc?

We keep getting subtle PD/ENG feedback about users losing context when they drill between models, routes, and rollout variants. Current left-rail + page title approach works for many flows but fails for: nested admin flows (rollouts -> canary -> nodes), deep resource views (dedicated pools -> instance -> logs), and quick shareable links where the left rail is collapsed in small viewports. This doc proposes a lightweight breadcrumb model (top-level context + micro-context) and a matched heading strategy that is consistent across pages and resilient to left-rail state. Also includes wireframe notes for desktop and mobile and a backlog grooming list.

Core goals (short):
- Make primary context explicit in the page chrome so that deep links and compact viewports communicate location clearly.
- Preserve task-oriented headings (what the user does here) while retaining resource identity (which model/pool, etc.).
- Keep breadcrumbs shallow (2-3 segments) — avoid long paths that duplicate left-rail.
- Ensure accessibility: semantic headings, skip targets, and announced breadcrumbs for screen readers.

Principles driving decisions:
- Less is more: breadcrumbs should be a quick, scannable context bar, not a full-trail sitemap.
- Dual-purpose headings: combine resource identity + task when useful (e.g., "Model: Llama-4 — Edit routing").
- Left rail is navigation; breadcrumbs are context. Do not replicate navigation hierarchy verbatim.
- Mobile first: when left rail collapses, breadcrumb + heading must suffice to orient.

Proposed breadcrumb model (rules):
1) Two-tier pattern: [Surface] > [Micro-context]. Surface = product area (Console, Models, Dedicated, Logs, Settings). Micro-context = resource or task (Model name, Pool name, Rollout).
   - Examples: "Models > Llama-4"; "Dedicated > Pool-alpha"; "Console > Usage".
2) If deeper drill-down required, surface the additional state inside the page body (subheading row or contextual chip group) instead of extending breadcrumb.
3) Breadcrumb links should always point to a stable collection or overview (Models overview, Dedicated pools list), not ephemeral filtered views.
4) When left rail is collapsed, show a minimal chevron breadcrumb (Surface > Micro). When left rail is open, show breadcrumbs but low-visual-weight (muted, small).
5) Support an optional "path hint" pill on hover for complex flows (dev-only; toggled behind flag).

Heading strategy (semantic + UX):
- H1: primary task or resource identity. Example: "Llama-4 — Model details" or "Create rollout for Pool-alpha". Keep H1 under 60 chars where possible.
- H2: contextual actions or status summary. Example: "Active variant: v2 (96% traffic) — 3 nodes". H2 doubles as a quick status panel for monitoring pages.
- Subsections: use H3/H4 for sections like Config, Metrics, Logs. Always include an anchor id for deep-linking and easier anchor copying.
- Accessibility: H1 should be focusable via "Skip to main heading" link; breadcrumb is role=navigation with aria-label="Breadcrumbs" and aria-current="page" for last item.

Wireframe notes (desktop):
- Top chrome: narrow breadcrumb bar (24px height) above H1. Breadcrumb text small + muted, chevrons 8px. Right side: quick actions (share, copy link, favorite).
- H1 area: left-aligned H1 with optional resource tags (e.g., private, prod). Right-aligned: primary CTA (Edit, Deploy) + small overflow menu.
- In-page context strip: immediately below H1, show a thin strip with 2-3 contextual chips (variant, region, traffic) which are interactive filters. These chips contain secondary navigation for nested views rather than extending the breadcrumb.
- Example flow: Models > Llama-4 (breadcrumb)
  H1: Llama-4 — Model details
  Context chips: [Version: v2] [Region: eu-west] [Routing: weighted]
  Tabs: Overview | Metrics | Rollouts | Deployments. Tabs remain unchanged.

Wireframe notes (mobile):
- Left rail collapsed. Top shows a single-line breadcrumb with truncated micro-context (ellipsis) and an affordance to expand to full resource selector.
- H1 is bold, single line; context chips collapse into a single overflow chip ("2 context items").
- Back button behavior: top-left back returns to previous list if user arrived via navigation; if landed directly (deep link), back should route to overview. This requires router awareness (see dependencies).

Routing mapping (high level):
- /models -> Breadcrumb: Models > (none). H1: Models
- /models/:id -> Breadcrumb: Models > :id. H1: :id — Model details
- /models/:id/rollouts/:rid -> Breadcrumb: Models > :id. H1: Rollout :rid for :id (context chips show rollout stage)
- /dedicated/pools -> Breadcrumb: Dedicated > Pools. H1: Dedicated pools
- /dedicated/pools/:pid/instances/:iid/logs -> Breadcrumb: Dedicated > Pool :pid. H1: Instance :iid logs
Notes: Breadcrumbs intentionally omit the full intermediate segments for long paths (eg. omit "instances" segment and surface it in H1).

Backlog grooming (candidate tickets):
- JIRA-1307: breadcrumb component, accessible markup + mobile collapse behavior (AC below).
- JIRA-1311: H1 + context-chip design system tokens and variants.
- JIRA-1315: router heuristics for back-button behavior on deep links.
- JIRA-1320: wireframe -> React prototypes for Models and Dedicated pages.
- JIRA-1333: analytics events and telemetry for breadcrumb clicks and context-chip interactions.

Acceptance criteria (for JIRA-1307):
- Breadcrumb renders correct Surface and Micro-context for the five mapped routes.
- Breadcrumb uses role=navigation and exposes aria-current on last item.
- Collapsed mobile breadcrumb shows a single-line truncated micro-context with expand affordance.
- Unit tests exist for accessible labels and snapshot testing.

Dependencies / cross-team notes:
- Router team: need a tiny API to surface "navigation origin" (deep link vs in-app nav) so back-button heuristics work. (Ping @Elliot - SRE/router).
- Design tokens: need small chip and breadcrumb tokens added to the theme (Ping @Marco - DX).
- Analytics: mapping of click events to new component names (Ping @Sofia - Growth).

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How much should breadcrumbs link vs be informational only? Lean toward links (overview is useful), but some admins worry about accidental context switches. Could gate link behavior behind "press-and-hold" UX for dangerous pages.
- Do we ever show user-level context (org -> project -> resource)? For now, surface org only when multi-org users created.
- Should the breadcrumb include icons? Pros: faster scanning, cons: visual noise on dense pages. Recommend icons only for surface level and hidden via user prefs.

Next steps (short-term):
1) Ship JIRA-1307 skeleton component (a11y + mobile collapse) as a feature-flagged component. (2-week spike).
2) Designer wireframes for Models & Dedicated pages + token handoff (Marco).
3) Engineering spike on router origin heuristics (Elliot).
4) Prototype in storybook and run quick usability sessions with 3 PMs/SREs (Sofia to coordinate).

Notes-to-self / rough todos:
- Add example aria labels to the component README.
- Draft short copy guidelines for H1s (verb-first when action-oriented).
- Add test case: deep link -> expand breadcrumb -> copy link -> lands at same state.

References / related docs:
- confluence:console-ia-v2 (bigger IA mapping)
- GitHub PR 482 (old left-rail refactor)
- JIRA-1280 (left rail collapse animation spec)

If this doc looks good, I will split into: 
- implementation spec (JIRA-1307) with CSS tokens and accessibility checklist
- designer handoff file (frames)
- prototype PR note with acceptance tests

End.
